newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine sees '97 beet output up to 30-31 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine sees '97 beet output up to 30-31 mln T.

text.p: Ukraine has forecast a sugar beet crop of 30 to 31 million tonnes in 1997, up from 24 million tonnes in 1996, Deputy Economy Minister Valentyn Poshyvailo said on Wednesday.

"It won't be a bad harvest, but of course we will see when we gather it," he told a news conference, offering the forecasts and saying that beet sowing reached 1.1 million hectares this year compared with 1.3 million last year.
Poshyvailo said yields were 3.0 tonnes per hectare at the start of this month, compared to 2.8 tonnes at the same time last year.

Previous government forecasts put the sugar beet crop at 24 million tonnes, but Poshyvailo said more favourable weather conditions had set in compared to last year, when a drought at the beginning of the growing season damaged plants.
Sugar beets in Ukraine, which produced 3.26 million tonnes of refined sugar last year, are traditionally harvested in September and October.
Russia is a major refined sugar export outlet for Ukraine.
Ukraine has forecast flat white sugar output.
